claims.text: The baseline eutectic high-entropy alloy has dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Optimized processing techniques can produce a refined microstructure.
The proposed microstructure will have a more uniform and refined lamellar-colony structure.
The proposed microstructure will contain fewer internal boundaries than the baseline.
Reducing internal boundaries will decrease microcrack initiation.
Reducing internal boundaries and making the microstructure more uniform will decrease microcrack propagation.
Decreased microcrack initiation and propagation will improve room-temperature tensile ductility.
Refining the lamellar-colony structure will maintain or increase tensile strength.
The intervention will improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The intervention is expected to be effective under room-temperature tensile deformation.
The intervention may not be applicable at high temperatures or under other extreme conditions.
The extent of strength and ductility improvement may depend on the processing technique and resulting microstructure.
